title: useR! 2025 Keywords Network
text: This interactive project explores how keywords were used across sessions at the useR! 2025 conference. The goal was to analyse and visualise how topics clustered together using text mining and network analysis techniques.

title: useR! 2025 Keywords Network
text:
Tools & Data Preparation
This analysis used the following R libraries:

tidyverse for data manipulation
tidytext for splitting keywords and keyword processing
widyr for calculating pairwise keyword co-occurrence
ggraph, igraph, and tidygraph for network visualization
shiny for interactivity

To prepare the data:

The dataset was cleaned by separating comma-separated keywords into individual rows
Extra whitespace and missing values were removed
Session-level keyword groupings were constructed using unite() and pairwise_count()
The final result was a co-occurrence network, where nodes are keywords and edges represent how often they appeared together in a session

title: useR! 2025 Keywords Network
text:
What I noticed
Shiny and APIs turned up together more often than any other pair of keywords, in three separate sessions. It’s a nice reminder that people are using Shiny as a front end for other services, not just for standalone dashboards.
AI sits right in the middle of the network. It connects LLMs, automation, data science and Shiny, which says a lot about what was on people’s minds at the conference this year.
Some topics travel in tight little groups of their own: DuckDB, big data and Parquet; Quarto and teaching; and ggplot2 with data visualisation.

title: Seismic Activity Dashboard
text:
What I noticed
Has activity changed over time? Yes, and quite a lot. 2013 and 2014 were the quiet years. Things picked up from 2015, peaked between 2018 and 2020, eased off slightly for a few years, and then 2024 was the busiest year of all.
Are events getting deeper? Not really. Nearly everything happens in the top kilometre, and below 3 km the events are few and far between. The deeper ones are rare but recent though: the only events in the 9 to 10 km band were in 2024.

title: RFDS Network Visualisation
text:
What I noticed
Brisbane was by far the busiest destination, with 52 arrivals in the month. Rockhampton (36) and Bundaberg (34) came next, then there’s a big drop to places like Charleville, which only had 2.
The part that stayed with me is how much of this work happens at night. Close to half of Brisbane’s arrivals (25 of 52) landed between 6pm and 6am, and the pattern is similar at Rockhampton and Cairns. Emergencies don’t keep office hours, and the flight logs show it.

title: Healthcare Australia Dashboard
text:
What I noticed
On the surface the numbers look reassuring: 93.7% of elective surgery patients were treated within the recommended time. But the average hides some very long waits. Excision of exostosis stood out at 455 days, well over a year.
Where you live makes a difference too. The ACT had the highest wait pressure of any state, about 55 days longer than the state with the shortest waits.
And the trend isn’t going the right way. Wait-time performance is getting worse over time, so this is something to keep an eye on rather than a one-off.

title: Mysticase: Side Business
text:
Where Data Meets Design
Mysticase was a small creative side business I co-launched on Etsy to explore how analytics and design come together in real-world ecommerce.
As a side project, Mysticase allowed me to use the analytical skills I gained during my Master’s to explore the intersection of design, data, and online retail.

title: Mysticase: Side Business
section: What I did as part of Mysticase:
text:
What I did as part of Mysticase:

Created all product imagery with design tools and automated mockup generation.

Used Etsy SEO strategies including keyword testing, titles, and tags.

Regularly reviewed analytics to improve conversion and discover trends.

Used Google Trends and Etsy search data to target low-competition niches.
Built lightweight workflows to automate Etsy listing creation and dynamic pricing updates.

title: Mysticase: Side Business
text:
Performance Overview




Mysticase Store Metrics: 2,000+ visits and $1,500+ in revenue





Mysticase Reach Metrics: 200+ favourites and 32 cities reached




It was never meant to be a large-scale commercial business, but rather an agile side project to:

Apply marketing data analytics in a practical setting

Understand customer behavior and analyse through real-time data

Develop SEO and product strategy based on insights showcasing insights analysis skills
Communicating through both data and design

This initiative was a fun, self-directed application of the skills I developed during my data analytics Master’s — and a way to keep learning creatively outside work. The shop has since closed, but the lessons in SEO, conversion analysis and product strategy carry into my analytics work today.

I’m a data analyst in Melbourne, and I think in patterns. Give me a spreadsheet, a dashboard or a half-finished dataset and I’ll go looking for the story that’s actually worth acting on.
I did my Master of Business Analytics at Monash, and most recently worked as a Customer Data Analyst at Comprara. There I was the sole analyst on a CRM clean-up: I brought 17,554 company records down to 11,749, linked 38,171 contacts to the right company and built the industry and job-role segments the team used for campaigns. Before that I co-founded Mysticase, a small Etsy business, and looked after the data side of it, from Google Trends research to listing and pricing decisions.
Outside of work I keep practising across industries through my 30 Days, 30 Industries challenge and TidyTuesday, building dashboards in R Shiny, Tableau and Power BI and writing up what I find in Quarto.
I’m looking for roles where I can bring together data analysis, customer insight, reporting and stakeholder communication to make a measurable difference.

title: Retail Executive Dashboard
text:
Key Insights

Electronics is the leading revenue category, generating the highest share of total revenue and acting as the main commercial revenue driver.
Category roles differ clearly: Electronics leads revenue, Clothing leads purchase volume, and Beauty has the highest average order value.
Sales performance appears more volume-driven than basket-size driven, suggesting that growth efforts should focus on traffic, conversion, and units per order.
May 2023 was the strongest sales month, making it a useful benchmark for planning future promotions, stock availability, and campaign timing.
Female customers contributed slightly more revenue than male customers, while the 45–54 age group emerged as the strongest age-based revenue segment.

title: Retail Executive Dashboard
text:
Business Recommendations

Prioritise Electronics in revenue-focused campaigns, homepage placements, and stock availability planning.
Use category-specific strategies: protect Electronics revenue, use Clothing for volume-led promotions, and position Beauty as a premium basket-value opportunity.
Focus sales initiatives on increasing traffic, conversion, and units per order, rather than relying only on higher prices.
Review the strongest month, May 2023, to understand what drove the performance and apply those learnings to future campaign planning.

title: RFDS Queensland Flight Network using D3.js
text:
This D3.js project explores Royal Flying Doctor Service (RFDS) flight routes and base activity within Queensland, using flight logs from July 2022.
The map highlights:

title: RFDS Queensland Flight Network using D3.js
text:
Resource

GitHub Repository

Analysis performed using D3.js and JavaScript, and the visualisation was built using SVG elements.

title: RFDS Queensland Flight Network using D3.js
text:
What I noticed
Once Brisbane is taken out of the picture, Townsville is clearly the centre of the regional network. It had 98 arrivals and departures in the month, more than any other base, and three of the four busiest routes run into it: from Cairns, Mount Isa and Mackay.
Mount Isa to Townsville is the route that surprised me. It was flown 26 times, and each trip is close to 780 km.
The longest route on the map is Townsville to Horn Island in the Torres Strait, around 1,080 km. And most of the dots aren’t bases at all: 36 of the 45 airports are smaller regional and remote airstrips the aircraft fly in and out of.

title: NSF Grant Terminations Analysis
text:
This interactive Shiny app explores patterns in early terminations of NSF-funded research projects. The analysis focuses on both individual project timelines and geographical trends across U.S. states.
Key questions investigated:

title: NSF Grant Terminations Analysis
text:
Grant Termination Timeline

Question
How long do NSF projects typically run before termination, and how early are they ended relative to their planned duration?


Approach

Built an interactive Gantt chart
Users select a directorate to view its projects
Start = project start date

End = actual termination date

Dotted line = expected end date

title: NSF Grant Terminations Analysis
text:
Termination Hotspots Across U.S. States

Question
Which U.S. states had the highest number of terminated NSF grants?


Approach

Created a choropleth heatmap of terminations by state
Users can click on a state to see a bar chart of organizations with terminations

title: NSF Grant Terminations Analysis
text:
Interactive Dashboard






 View the GitHub repo
 See my LinkedIn post

title: NSF Grant Terminations Analysis
text:
What I noticed
The timeline view makes the answer to “how early?” hard to miss. In Biological Sciences, almost every grant was cut on the same date in spring 2025, and many of them still had one to three years left to run.
On the map, California is the darkest state by a clear margin, with Texas and New York next.
Clicking into a state tells a more concentrated story. Colorado had 39 terminations, and the University of Colorado Boulder alone accounts for more than half of them. For some states, a handful of institutions carry most of the impact.

title: Measles Outbreak Insights
text: This project investigates global measles outbreak data using the TidyTuesday 24-06-2025 dataset, analysed on 25-06-2025. Using WHO provisional reports from 2015–2025, the analysis highlights vulnerable countries, under-reported outbreaks, and population-level immunisation challenges.

title: Measles Outbreak Insights
text:
Key Features

 Seasonal Heatmap of monthly outbreak patterns for top countries.
 Bubble Chart showing vaccine coverage gaps for large populations
 Scatter Plot to detect under-reporting by comparing incidence and totals

title: Measles Outbreak Insights
text:
Interactive Report
Hover over the bubbles in Bubble chart to learn more:

title: Measles Outbreak Insights
text:
Key Insights

Seasonal patterns show distinct outbreak peaks across regions, supporting the need for region-specific vaccination timing.
High-incidence countries like Madagascar, Mongolia, and Kyrgyzstan had relatively low total case counts, suggesting possible under-reporting.
The scatter plot revealed several countries with inconsistent surveillance, highlighting a gap in global health reporting systems.
Countries with low vaccine coverage and large populations such as Nigeria and Pakistan are critical priorities for public health interventions.
The bubble chart enabled identification of outlier regions where vaccine programs may not be translating into coverage or protection, warranting further investigation.
